# Story 05 — Admin Hall Management (Story: 5)

## Prerequisites

- Story 04 (admin dashboard / admin shell) must be completed: the `admin` feature area, `admin.routes.ts`, `admin-layout` shell, and the `adminGuard` route guard must already exist and be wired into `app.routes.ts`. Confirm this by inspecting `src/app/features/admin/admin.routes.ts` and `src/app/core/auth/admin.guard.ts` before starting.
- Reuses the authenticated `HttpClient` flow already established by `src/app/core/auth/auth.interceptor.ts` (attaches the auth token to outgoing requests) and the login/session state exposed by `src/app/core/auth/auth.service.ts`. No changes to auth are required for this story — halls management only consumes the existing authenticated `HttpClient`.
- Follows the same admin CRUD pattern intended for `src/app/features/admin/movies/` (currently a placeholder stub) and `src/app/features/admin/screenings/` (also a placeholder stub) — this story is the first to actually flesh out an admin CRUD feature end-to-end, so keep the structure generic enough that Movies/Screenings admin stories can copy it later.
- Mirrors the read-model pattern already used for the public-facing `src/app/features/movies/services/movie.service.ts` and `src/app/features/movies/models/movie.model.ts` (HttpClient-based service returning typed models) — read those two files in full before writing the hall service, since they are small (under 1 KB each) and establish the HttpClient injection / base-path conventions used elsewhere in this project.
- Mirrors the signal-based UI state pattern used in `src/app/features/reservation/services/reservation-state.service.ts` (6.7 KB) for exposing loading/error/data state to components via Angular signals — read this file in full to match its signal-based state-exposure style (loading signal, error signal, data signal, and methods that mutate them around HTTP calls).

## Story Goal

Deliver a full admin Cinema Hall Management feature in the Angular frontend:

1. An authenticated administrator can list all halls at `/admin/halls`, see title, seat count, type, active/inactive status, and created date, with loading/empty/error states and retry.
2. An administrator can view a single hall's details.
3. An administrator can create a hall via `/admin/halls/create` with client-side validation (title required, seat count required and > 0, type required and restricted to the supported enum) before submit.
4. An administrator can edit an existing hall via `/admin/halls/{id}/edit`, pre-populated from `GET /api/halls/{id}`, submitted via `PUT /api/halls/{id}`.
5. An administrator can deactivate an active hall (confirmation dialog, then `PATCH /api/halls/{id}/deactivate`) and activate an inactive hall (confirmation dialog, then `PATCH /api/halls/{id}/activate`), with the list/details view updating in place afterward.
6. All HTTP failures (400/401/403/404/409/500) are translated into user-friendly messages; raw backend exception bodies are never rendered directly.

**Not in scope:** any change to backend authorization enforcement (backend is authoritative), any change to how screenings consume halls (that belongs to a Screenings admin story — this story only ensures the hall list/edit UI itself does not present inactive halls as if they were active), and any change to the shared `auth` module or `admin.guard.ts` route-protection mechanism.

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Hall domain model

**Create file: `src/app/features/admin/halls/hall.models.ts`**

Define the domain types matching the backend contract described in the intake (`Id`, `Title`, `NumberOfSeats`, `Type`, `IsActive`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`) and the supported hall types (`Standard`, `4D`, `Gold`, `MAX`, `IMAX`). Mirror the plain-interface style found in `src/app/features/movies/models/movie.model.ts`.

```typescript
export type HallType = 'Standard' | '4D' | 'Gold' | 'MAX' | 'IMAX';

export const HALL_TYPES: HallType[] = ['Standard', '4D', 'Gold', 'MAX', 'IMAX'];

export interface Hall {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  numberOfSeats: number;
  type: HallType;
  isActive: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
}

export interface CreateHallRequest {
  title: string;
  numberOfSeats: number;
  type: HallType;
}

export interface UpdateHallRequest {
  title: string;
  numberOfSeats: number;
  type: HallType;
}
```

Adjust the `id` type to `number` if, after reading `src/app/features/movies/models/movie.model.ts`, the existing `Movie` model uses numeric ids for consistency with the rest of the project — match whatever convention that file uses.

### 2 — Hall service

**Create file: `src/app/features/admin/halls/hall.service.ts`**

Follow the exact `HttpClient` injection and base-path construction pattern used in `src/app/features/movies/services/movie.service.ts` (read in Context step 4 before writing this). Expose one method per backend endpoint from the intake:

```typescript
import { Injectable, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { HttpClient } from '@angular/common/http';
import { Observable } from 'rxjs';
import { CreateHallRequest, Hall, UpdateHallRequest } from './hall.models';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class HallService {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);
  private readonly baseUrl = '/api/halls'; // match the base-path convention read from movie.service.ts

  getHalls(): Observable<Hall[]> {
    return this.http.get<Hall[]>(this.baseUrl);
  }

  getHall(id: string): Observable<Hall> {
    return this.http.get<Hall>(`${this.baseUrl}/${id}`);
  }

  createHall(request: CreateHallRequest): Observable<Hall> {
    return this.http.post<Hall>(this.baseUrl, request);
  }

  updateHall(id: string, request: UpdateHallRequest): Observable<Hall> {
    return this.http.put<Hall>(`${this.baseUrl}/${id}`, request);
  }

  deactivateHall(id: string): Observable<Hall> {
    return this.http.patch<Hall>(`${this.baseUrl}/${id}/deactivate`, {});
  }

  activateHall(id: string): Observable<Hall> {
    return this.http.patch<Hall>(`${this.baseUrl}/${id}/activate`, {});
  }
}
```

**Do not** hardcode a full origin — reuse whatever base-URL/environment convention `movie.service.ts` uses (relative path vs. an `environment.apiBaseUrl`). If `movie.service.ts` references an environment file, add the equivalent `/api/halls` constant there instead of inlining it, and cite the exact environment file path once found.

### 3 — Hall list component

**Create file: `src/app/features/admin/halls/hall-list/hall-list.component.ts`** (+ `.html`, `.css`, `.spec.ts`)

Standalone component, injected `HallService`. Expose signals mirroring the state-exposure idiom read from `reservation-state.service.ts`:

- `halls = signal<Hall[]>([])`
- `loading = signal<boolean>(true)`
- `error = signal<string | null>(null)`
- `filter = signal<'all' | 'active' | 'inactive'>('all')` — a local computed/filtered view over `halls()` (since the intake states the frontend may filter client-side if the backend does not support a query filter — confirm during implementation whether `GET /api/halls` accepts a query parameter; if it does, pass it through instead of filtering client-side).

On `ngOnInit`, call `hallService.getHalls()`, set `loading` false and populate `halls` on success, or set a friendly `error` message on failure (map HTTP status per the error-handling task below — do not display `err.message` directly).

Template (`hall-list.component.html`) renders:
- Loading state: a simple loading indicator while `loading()` is true.
- Empty state: the exact copy `"No cinema halls have been created yet."` when `halls().length === 0` and not loading/error.
- Error state with a **Retry** button that re-invokes the load method.
- A table with columns: Title, Number of Seats, Type, Status (Active/Inactive badge), Created date (`createdAt`, formatted with Angular `DatePipe`), and an Actions column with **View**, **Edit**, and a single **Deactivate**/**Activate** button that toggles per-row based on `hall.isActive` (per the intake's "please do the opposite for activate hall and adjust the interface" instruction).
- A toggle/segmented control for the Active/Inactive/All filter described above.

Deactivate/Activate actions must show a confirmation prompt first (`window.confirm` is acceptable given no dialog/modal library exists elsewhere in this codebase — confirm by checking whether any `Confirm`/`Dialog` component already exists under `src/app/shared/`; if none exists, use `window.confirm` with the exact copy pattern `"Are you sure you want to deactivate {title}?"` / `"Are you sure you want to activate {title}?"`), then call `hallService.deactivateHall(id)` / `activateHall(id)`, and on success update the row's `isActive` in the `halls` signal in place (do not remove the row) and show a success message (a simple inline banner/toast consistent with whatever success-message convention exists in `register.component.ts`/`login.component.ts` — reuse that same mechanism rather than inventing a new one).

### 5 — Reusable hall form component

**Create file: `src/app/features/admin/halls/hall-form/hall-form.component.ts`** (+ `.html`, `.css`, `.spec.ts`)

A shared standalone component accepting an optional `@Input() hall: Hall | null` (null for create mode, populated for edit mode) and emitting `@Output() formSubmit = new EventEmitter<CreateHallRequest>()`. Build the `FormGroup` with `FormBuilder` mirroring the construction style in `src/app/features/auth/register/register.component.ts` (read in Context step 11):

```typescript
this.form = this.fb.group({
  title: ['', [Validators.required]],
  numberOfSeats: [null, [Validators.required, Validators.min(1)]],
  type: ['', [Validators.required]],
});
```

- `Validators.min(1)` enforces "greater than zero" for `numberOfSeats` (paired with `Validators.required` since `0` is falsy but a valid `min` check).
- The `type` field is a `<select>` bound to `HALL_TYPES` from `hall.models.ts`, so only supported values are selectable — this satisfies "Hall type must be one of the supported values" without a custom validator.
- Disable the submit button while `form.invalid` or while a submission is in flight (mirror the `isSubmitting` boolean/signal pattern from `register.component.ts`).
- Accept and render a `@Input() serverError: string | null` so the parent (create/edit component) can pass through backend validation error messages (400/409 responses) without the form inventing its own copy.

### 9 — Error handling

Add a small shared mapping helper (either a private method reused across the three new components/service, or — preferred, to avoid duplication — a function in `src/app/features/admin/halls/hall.models.ts` or a new `hall-error.util.ts` in the same folder) that converts an `HttpErrorResponse` status code into one user-friendly string, per the intake's required matrix:

| Status | Message |
|---|---|
| 400 | "The hall details entered are invalid. Please check the form and try again." |
| 401 | "Your session has expired. Please sign in again." |
| 403 | "You do not have permission to manage cinema halls." |
| 404 | "The requested hall could not be found." |
| 409 | "This hall could not be saved because of a conflict with existing data." |
| 500 / other | "Something went wrong. Please try again later." |

Never interpolate `error.error.message` or any raw backend body text into these strings — only use it to decide *which* of the fixed messages above to show for 400/409 if the backend includes field-level validation detail (optional refinement: if `error.error` contains a `message` string, prefer displaying that specific string only for 400/409, still without exposing 500-class internals).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty hall list** — `GET /api/halls` returns `[]`: `hall-list.component` must render the exact empty-state copy `"No cinema halls have been created yet."` instead of an empty table, enforced in the list component's template conditional (Task 3).
- **Network/server failure on initial list load** — `hall-list.component` must show the error state with a **Retry** button that re-calls `getHalls()`, not a blank/broken table (Task 3, Task 9 mapping table).
- **Deactivating an already-inactive hall (409) or activating an already-active hall (409)** — surfaced via the shared 409 message from Task 9; the acting row/detail view must not optimistically flip status until the HTTP call actually succeeds.
- **Edit route loaded with a nonexistent id (404)** — `hall-edit.component` and `hall-details.component` must show the mapped 404 message and a link back to `/admin/halls`, not a blank form (Task 4, Task 7).
- **Submitting create/edit form with `numberOfSeats = 0` or negative** — must be blocked client-side by `Validators.min(1)` before any HTTP call is made (Task 5); confirm the submit button stays disabled and no `POST`/`PUT` fires.
- **Submitting create/edit form with an unsupported `type` value** — prevented structurally by constraining the `<select>` options to `HALL_TYPES` (Task 5), so no client-side value outside the enum can ever be submitted.
- **Backend validation failure on submit (400)** — the form's `serverError` input must render the mapped message from Task 9 without navigating away, so the admin can correct and resubmit (Task 6, Task 7).
- **Unauthorized/forbidden access (401/403)** — since `admin.routes.ts` is already guarded by `adminGuard` (Context step 8), a non-admin should never reach these components; nonetheless, an expired session mid-session (token expiring while the halls page is open) must still be handled by the 401 mapping in Task 9 rather than crashing the component.
- **Deactivated hall still needing to be visible** — the list/details components must never filter out inactive halls by default from the underlying `halls` signal; only the optional Active/Inactive/All display filter (Task 3) hides rows, and switching the filter back to "All" or "Inactive" must still show them with their full historical data intact.
- **Race between navigating away and an in-flight create/update request** — ensure the create/edit components do not throw on component destruction mid-request (use `takeUntilDestroyed()` if that pattern already exists elsewhere in the codebase — verify by grepping for `takeUntilDestroyed` before introducing it, otherwise a simple subscription without teardown is acceptable given existing project conventions).

## Done Criteria

- [ ] Administrator can view all halls at `/admin/halls`, including title, seat count, type, status, and created date.
- [ ] Administrator can view a single hall's full details.
- [ ] Administrator can create a hall via `/admin/halls/create`, with the request sent as `POST /api/halls`.
- [ ] Administrator can edit a hall via `/admin/halls/{id}/edit`, pre-populated from `GET /api/halls/{id}` and submitted via `PUT /api/halls/{id}`.
- [ ] Hall type selection is restricted to `Standard`, `4D`, `Gold`, `MAX`, `IMAX`.
- [ ] Number of seats must be present and greater than zero before the create/edit form can be submitted.
- [ ] Title and hall type are required before the create/edit form can be submitted.
- [ ] Deactivating a hall requires a confirmation prompt, calls `PATCH /api/halls/{id}/deactivate`, and updates the displayed status without removing the hall.
- [ ] Activating a hall requires a confirmation prompt, calls `PATCH /api/halls/{id}/activate`, and updates the displayed status.
- [ ] Inactive halls remain visible (not hard-filtered out) in the list/details views, with a clear inactive marker.
- [ ] Backend 400/409 validation errors are displayed on the create/edit form via the mapped user-friendly messages.
- [ ] 401/403/404/500 responses across all hall screens show the mapped user-friendly messages, never raw backend text.
- [ ] Loading, empty, error (with retry), and success states are all implemented on the hall list screen.
- [ ] `/admin/halls*` routes remain reachable only through the existing `adminGuard`-protected `admin.routes.ts` tree.
